On the right side is a schematic diagram of the Earth’s motion around the Sun, used to indicate seasonal positions such as the equinoxes and solstices. Then reason: Dengfeng’s latitude is about 34°N. On the summer solstice, the latitude of the direct solar point is equal to the obliquity of the ecliptic ε, so the local noon solar altitude H=90°−34°+ε. If the obliquity of the ecliptic becomes smaller, then the latitude of the direct solar point on the summer solstice decreases, and Dengfeng’s noon solar altitude accordingly decreases. When the crossbeam height remains unchanged, the lower the solar altitude, the longer the noon shadow. On the summer solstice, Dengfeng’s noon Sun is still located in the southern sky, so the shadow is cast toward the long embankment directly north. Thus the crossbeam’s noon projection on the long embankment will move northward along the long embankment, and the shadow length will become longer.

On the right side is a schematic diagram of the Earth’s motion around the Sun, used to indicate seasonal positions such as the equinoxes and solstices. Then reason: Dengfeng’s latitude is about 34°N. On the summer solstice, the latitude of the direct solar point is equal to the obliquity of the ecliptic ε, so the local noon solar altitude H=90°−34°+ε. If the obliquity of the ecliptic becomes smaller, then the latitude of the direct solar point on the summer solstice decreases, and Dengfeng’s noon solar altitude accordingly decreases. When the crossbeam height remains unchanged, the lower the solar altitude, the longer the noon shadow. On the summer solstice, Dengfeng’s noon Sun is still located in the southern sky, so the shadow is cast toward the long embankment directly north. Thus the crossbeam’s noon projection on the long embankment will move northward along the long embankment, and the shadow length will become longer.
